gen_risks.description: Incomplete geotechnical studies may cause design changes and cost overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct comprehensive geotechnical investigations before final design and include cost contingency.
gen_risks.evidence: Incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies... resulting in design changes/variations during construction and consequently time and cost overruns.

gen_risks.description: Minimum environmental flow may not be maintained during dry season, harming downstream users and ecosystems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Install flow‑monitoring devices, design intakes with buffer storage, and enforce minimum‑EF compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: Namatala’s dry weather flows may not be sufficient... downstream users and aquatic biota could be affected if minimum EF is not maintained.

gen_risks.description: Leakage from sewers, sludge drying beds and wastewater ponds if O&M is inadequate.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict O&M protocols, periodic inspections, and rapid repair mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Leakages from sewers, sludge drying beds and wastewater stabilization ponds will be minimized by regular monitoring and maintenance.

gen_risks.description: Improper handling of asbestos‑cement pipes poses health and environmental hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Follow ESMF asbestos‑handling procedures and use certified disposal contractors.
gen_risks.evidence: For AC pipes, the Environmental Management Plan includes management measures for removal, packaging, transportation and disposal of existing asbestos waste.

gen_risks.description: Small‑dam safety risks due to inadequate design or inspection.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use qualified engineers, adhere to Small‑Dam Guidelines, and conduct independent safety audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Qualified engineers are used to design these dams; Small Dam Guidelines will be used to ensure adherence to generic dam safety measures.

gen_risks.description: Low technical expertise for solar‑powered water schemes may delay implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted technical assistance and capacity‑building workshops for solar pump installation.
gen_risks.evidence: The most important barrier to solar schemes is the low level of technical expertise on solar energy among WASH stakeholders.

gen_risks.description: Underestimation of construction costs leading to overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use detailed cost estimates, apply a contingency buffer, and monitor expenditures monthly.
gen_risks.evidence: Delayed construction and underestimation of the cost of works attributed to preparation of designs for works during the Project life.

gen_risks.description: Revenue collection may be insufficient where tariffs do not cover costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Review and adjust tariffs, improve billing systems, and strengthen revenue‑collection mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: In some regions, cost recovery is not achieved. The NWSC’s financial analysis shows tariffs cover O&M but not investment costs.

gen_risks.description: Debt service on the IDA loan could strain NWSC cash flow.
gen_risks.mitigation: Phase loan repayments, maintain cost‑recovery ratios above 1.1, and explore refinancing options.
gen_risks.evidence: Annual payments of principal and service charge would correspond to less than 1.4 % of total annual revenues after 2025.

gen_risks.description: UWAs depend on donor subsidies for capital investments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a revolving financing facility and progressive tariff policy to build internal funding.
gen_risks.evidence: UWAs are still dependent on public financing for capital investments and for providing assistance on O&M related‑activities.

gen_risks.description: Procurement delays due to PDU staff’s lack of experience and heavy workload.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a procurement consultant experienced with World Bank rules and provide on‑the‑job training.
gen_risks.evidence: PDU staff have no experience in using World Bank Procurement Regulations and have a heavy workload.

gen_risks.description: Delays in preparing specifications and Terms of Reference.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign dedicated technical officers to draft ToRs early and set firm internal deadlines.
gen_risks.evidence: Delays in preparing specifications, statement of requirements, and ToRs by the User Departments.

gen_risks.description: Vendor payments delayed by internal approval bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a payment‑tracking system with clear SLA for approvals and senior management oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: Delays in paying vendors due to delays in internal approving processes.

gen_risks.description: Staff turnover reduces institutional memory and continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer retention incentives, document procedures, and ensure knowledge‑transfer hand‑over plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Turnover of qualified and experienced staff is noticed.

gen_risks.description: Large refugee influx increases pressure on water resources and host communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Coordinate with UNHCR for joint water‑service planning and scale up infrastructure with buffer capacity.
gen_risks.evidence: An estimated one million South Sudanese refugees have already migrated to Uganda… pressure on Uganda’s public services and natural resources.

gen_risks.description: Long water‑collection distances increase gender‑based violence risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Locate water points within 200 m of households and run gender‑sensitive awareness campaigns.
gen_risks.evidence: Women and girls bear the heaviest burden for water collection. Long walks… trigger serious social consequences, including GBV.

gen_risks.description: Labor influx may lead to GBV and other social issues.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include a Labour‑Influx Management Plan, enforce contractor code‑of‑conduct, and monitor compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: Measures to address labour influx include a code of conduct… to minimize any potential GBV in the Project areas.

gen_risks.description: Coordination challenges among multiple agencies could cause delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen the PST, schedule regular inter‑agency meetings, and use a shared project‑management platform.
gen_risks.evidence: Given the number of departments… the WESLD will take responsibility for overall coordination and communication.

gen_risks.description: Regional instability from the South‑Sudan conflict threatens project execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain security monitoring, develop contingency scenarios, and keep implementation schedules flexible.
gen_risks.evidence: The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑change‑induced floods and droughts threaten water‑supply reliability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilient designs, catchment protection, flood‑proof structures, and early‑warning systems.
gen_risks.evidence: A high‑level screening… extreme temperature… increase in precipitation… likely to cause floods.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk: as detailed in the CPF, significant political uncertainty is not foreseen, but governance and effective public-sector management present substantial risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will mitigate these risks through (a) strengthening the MWE's regulatory framework; (b) carrying out a citizen engagement strategy; and (c) strengthening project implementation efforts in close coordination with local government officials and development partners. The World Bank's procurement processes will also help safeguard the Project from corruption.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk: the Umbrella Water Authority (UWA) as a regional service delivery model for small towns and RGCs was recently introduced. Although the decision to scale up this model was informed by extensive analytical work and a pilot project, the UWA model was only recently operationalized.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will support implementation of a professionalized monitoring system focused on enhancing revenue collection approaches (billing software, cashless/mobile payment systems) and on strengthening integration of specialized private operators through improved contract management. The implementation team will use the Utility Performance Monitoring and Information System (UPMIS) tool to regularly review UWA and NWSC performance.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk: the Procurement risk is rated Substantial while the FM risk is Moderate. The risks identified relate to delays and skills gaps at different stages of procurement processing.
gt_risks.mitigation: IWMDP will benefit from the lessons learned and mechanisms put in place under the predecessor project (WMDP); detailed mitigation measures for the procurement risk are set out in the Appraisal (Procurement) section.

gt_risks.description: The environmental and social risk is deemed Substantial given (a) potential opposition to the introduction of a new service delivery model, including new tariffs and catchment management measures; (b) the influx of new workers in small towns and RGCs; and (c) potentially adverse environmental impacts from the construction and operation of the proposed investments.
gt_risks.mitigation: The environmental and social risk will be managed through the application of an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and related safeguards instruments (Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Resettlement Action Plans).

gt_risks.description: Other risks (social tensions in districts hosting refugees): tensions between refugees and citizens are caused by inequity in access to and payment for water supply and sanitation (WSS) services. While refugees in the settlements benefit from humanitarian aid and GoU support, Ugandans in host communities receive limited support for services and infrastructure, causing social tension that may result in Project implementation delays given potential community opposition to the works.
gt_risks.mitigation: The GoU has prioritized development efforts for poor districts hosting refugees while remaining firmly committed to its policy on refugee protection. The Project will manage this risk by designing WSS facilities and catchment management measures that benefit both host communities and refugees, and by ensuring the Project's social and communication management plan is applied and adequately supervised. There are no known existing risks to the refugee protection framework or reputational risks for the Project.
